 San Diego CPA sentenced to 18 months for $1.5 million tax fraud scheme

 SAN DIEGO — A local certified public accountant was sentenced in federal court Friday to 18 months in prison for preparing fraudulent tax returns that resulted in $1.5 million in losses to the federal government.
 Oladapo Olagbemi, 72, manager of the San Diego-based firm D.A.O. Accounting, Consulting, and Taxation, received the sentence after pleading guilty in June to four counts of aiding and assisting in the preparation of false tax returns.
 According to court documents, Olagbemi admitted to executing multiple schemes across tax years 2019 through 2023. He generated illegitimate tax refunds for clients by fabricating $5 million in improper deductions and tax credits, including phony business expenses, charitable contributions, and energy credits.
 Federal prosecutors emphasized that Olagbemi continued his fraudulent operations despite repeated interventions by law enforcement and regulatory bodies. He persisted in filing false returns after an investigation by the California Board of Accountancy, interviews with civil and criminal IRS agents, and a federal search of his office. Olagbemi even filed at least one false tax return after entering his guilty plea while awaiting sentencing.
 His practice was highly lucrative, generating nearly $1.2 million in gross revenue in 2025 alone.
 "He betrayed the trust of his clients," U.S. District Judge Ruth Bermudez Montenegro noted during the sentencing hearing.
 "Tax fraud may hide the truth for a moment, but justice always comes to collect," U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon said in a statement following the hearing.
 Darren Lian, Special Agent in Charge of the IRS Criminal Investigation's Los Angeles Field Office, condemned Olagbemi's brazen disregard for the law.
 "For years, Olagbemi abused his position as a trusted tax preparer by filing fraudulent returns designed to generate refunds to which his clients were not entitled," Lian said. "Even after being confronted by authorities and pleading guilty, he continued engaging in the same conduct. Today’s sentence demonstrates that individuals who undermine the integrity of our tax system for personal gain will be held accountable."
 Under federal law, each count of aiding and assisting in the preparation of false tax returns carries a maximum penalty of up to three years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, or twice the gross gain or loss.
